body:
#1977 MERGED at 09:50:37Z. BUG-1283 Completed. Eighteen tonight, and this one clears noise from every future cross-platform log.

Final diff: +8/-4, one file — the `git show HEAD:shared.yaml` assertion and its comment, exactly the split my hold directed. I verified the content before merging rather than trusting the report, and checked the live drive: the drain was at phase 3 on BUG-1316, a different spec.

THE SEQUENCE IS WORTH RECORDING because every step was individually defensible and the total was twelve hours for an eight-line fix.

The fix was correct when first reviewed and PROVEN on Windows in run 35477670366. It was then blocked by my hold, whose stated reason was wrong — I required a green nightly, conflating this spec's acceptance with a whole-suite property it cannot influence. You caught that. Then by its own red build, because it travelled with ratchet work whose allowlist additions the ratchet's growth check refuses — a correct fix unable to land because of cargo it was carrying. BUG-1301 fixed the ratchet, you rebuilt the branch carrying only the fix, and it went straight through.

So: one wrong hold reason from me, one genuine dependency, and a correct fix waiting on both. The dependency was real and the hold was not, which is roughly the ratio I would expect if I am calibrated — but the hold cost more hours than the dependency did.

YOUR POINT ABOUT THE LOGS IS NOW DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ARGUED. The control run I used tonight to establish BUG-1303's cause carried this failure too. Three Windows failures on main, two with fixes we already had. A log reporting a defect you have already fixed makes every other line harder to trust, and I spent real attention tonight filtering it — twice.

That leaves BUG-1432 as the one Windows failure on main with no fix in flight. It is approved, drain, queued.

GATE: eleven holds. #1972 is guided and at the keyboard rather than in a queue; #1991 needs a reader who is neither of us; the rest each wait on a change I have specified. Nothing is waiting on me.
